about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: Apollo Temple: the spec sheet (health, fitness and nutrition: workouts, steps, sleep, weight, meals, from Apple Health / Google Fit / the apps Joseph already uses)
tasks.why: Apollo Temple is a seat on the desk with no page yet. Joseph wants each pillar developed on its own; the first step is a spec Claude can build from.
steps: Write the spec for Apollo Temple: health, fitness and nutrition: workouts, steps, sleep, weight, meals, from Apple Health / Google Fit / the apps Joseph already uses.
At least 6 data sources with their real API names and documentation URLs (open each one); say plainly when something has no public API.
Four first screens, each listing every number on it and where it comes from.
Five 'done when' checks that can be tested on a phone.
Health data stays on the device or in Joseph's own accounts; say which sources can export without a server.

deliver.shape: one markdown file with these 6 headings, in this order: 1 Purpose (one sentence) | 2 Data sources (a table: source | what it gives | how to get it (API name) | docs URL | sign-in type | cost | limits) | 3 First four screens (for each: its name, every number and list on it, where each comes from) | 4 Version 1 done when (5 checks Claude can test) | 5 Privacy (what never leaves the device) | 6 What Joseph must do once (accounts, keys, apps)

tasks.done_when: All 6 headings, at least 6 sources with working docs URLs, 4 screens, 5 testable checks.
checks: Claude checks each 'done when' can be tested without asking Joseph.
rejected_if: a row copied from another row with the names changed
a source URL that does not open or does not say what the row claims
fewer items than the count
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
an API that does not exist or a docs URL for something else
a screen that lists a number with no source

tasks.title: 300 foods with their USDA FoodData Central numbers per 100 g
tasks.why: Apollo logs calories and protein; a food table from USDA (public domain) lets Joseph pick a food instead of typing numbers.
steps: Pick 300 foods an American eats (meats, fish, eggs, dairy, grains, breads, fruits, vegetables, legumes, nuts, oils, sweets, drinks, 30 fast-food items).

Use only Foundation or SR Legacy entries. For each: the FDC ID, the exact description, and per 100 g: energy (kcal), protein, total fat, carbohydrate, fiber (g), from https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/{FDC ID}/nutrients.
Save in 3 files of 100 rows (part1, part2, part3).

deliver.shape: [{"n":1,"fdc_id":171077,"description":"Chicken, broilers or fryers, breast, meat only, cooked, roasted","data_type":"SR Legacy","kcal":165,"protein_g":31.0,"fat_g":3.6,"carb_g":0,"fiber_g":0,"url":"https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/171077/nutrients"}]

tasks.done_when: 3 files, 300 foods, every FDC ID real.
checks: Claude checks 30 FDC IDs at random against the FoodData Central API (a value off by more than 2 % fails the row).
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a Branded entry
an FDC ID that does not match the description

tasks.title: 150 exercises with their Compendium of Physical Activities code and MET
tasks.why: Apollo can estimate calories from training only with a MET per activity; the 2024 Adult Compendium is the reference.
steps: 150 exercises and activities (lifts, machines, bodyweight, cardio machines, sports, walking and running speeds, yard and house work).

For each: the 2024 Adult Compendium code and MET value from pacompendium.com (the activity's own row), primary muscles, equipment, and one form cue from a named source (ACE exercise library, NSCA, or a physiotherapy source).
tasks.done_when: 150 rows, every code and MET from the Compendium.
checks: Claude checks 20 codes at random on pacompendium.com.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a MET from a calorie-calculator site

tasks.title: 40 health reference ranges from the guideline that sets them
tasks.why: Apollo's trends need lines to compare against (resting heart rate, blood pressure, sleep, steps, BMI, waist, protein per kg).
steps: 40 ranges, each from the body that sets it: AHA (blood pressure categories), CDC/WHO (activity minutes, BMI classes), AASM (adult sleep hours), USDA Dietary Guidelines (sodium, added sugar, fiber), NIH ODS (vitamin D, water), ACSM (training), etc.
For each: the metric, the unit, the bands with their numbers, the URL and the quote.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a range from a news article or a fitness blog

tasks.title: Android Health Connect: the 30 record types Apollo v2 would read
tasks.why: Joseph is on Android. Version 2 can read steps, sleep, weight and heart rate from Health Connect instead of typing them.
steps: From developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/androidx/health/connect/client/records/ list 30 record types (StepsRecord, SleepSessionRecord, WeightRecord, HeartRateRecord, ExerciseSessionRecord, NutritionRecord, HydrationRecord, RestingHeartRateRecord ...).
For each: the exact class name, the fields Apollo needs with their unit types, the read permission string (android.permission.health.READ_...), and the reference URL.
tasks.done_when: 30 record types, every class and permission exact.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a class or permission name that is not on its reference page

tasks.title: 25 meta-analyses on what keeps people training and eating to plan
tasks.why: Apollo's nudges (streaks, goals, reminders) should follow evidence, not vibes.
steps: 25 meta-analyses or systematic reviews (2010 or later) on adherence: self-monitoring, goal setting, habit formation, reminders, social support, streaks/gamification, implementation intentions.
For each: DOI, first author, year, number of studies and participants, the main effect with its number (effect size, odds ratio or percent), and one sentence of what Apollo should do because of it.
tasks.done_when: 25 papers, every DOI resolves to that paper.
checks: An effect with no number does not count.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a DOI that resolves to another paper
a single study instead of a meta-analysis or systematic review
